crowded_zones.avoid_reason: Over-signals generic AI-agent tooling and blends into a saturated orchestration category.
Low-distinctiveness prefix that dates quickly and sounds commodity.
Strongly occupied by LLM framework brands; likely to imply language-model plumbing.
Crowded by LLM and workflow sequence metaphors; can feel brittle or crypto-adjacent.
Tied to multi-agent team metaphors rather than proof-oriented execution.
Ubiquitous in workflow products and too soft for verification/trust positioning.
Direct graph language is heavily used and narrows perception to graph infrastructure.
Feels like generic task management rather than higher-level orchestration.
Automation prefix is saturated and can imply reckless autonomy.
Connotes chatbots and support automation, not dependable engineering workflows.
Common developer-tool metaphor with many existing projects and limited freshness.
Operational suffix/prefix feels enterprise-generic and category-bound.
Common execution-language zone; difficult to own and can sound infrastructure-only.
Useful semantic area but the literal prefix is crowded and can feel QA-only.
Legally and semantically dominated by assistant products; suggests sidekick UX rather than system control.
Premium but generic; often lacks memorable connection to artifacts, evidence, or convergence.
Can pass a domain screen but offers weak meaning and low recall among developer brands.

opportunity_zones.direction: Names that evoke evidence, certificates, manifests, seals, proofs, attestations, or reproducible records.
Craft language for connecting work across agents and tools without saying orchestration.
Compass, bearing, sextant, chart, waypoint, and course metaphors for directed execution.
Conductor, score, cadence, canon, measure, and harmony metaphors for coordinated independent parts.
Editorial proof, galley, edition, mark, and press language for reviewable outputs.
Node/edge alternatives such as lattice, mesh, adjacency, paths, spans, cuts, and joins.
Terms suggesting exact tolerances, joinery, gauges, calipers, fit, and finish.
Reliable records of transition, provenance, completion, and accountability.
Subtle network intelligence and distributed coordination without AI clichés.
Names around limits, closure, invariants, attractors, fixed points, and convergence.
Checkpoint, rite, closure, pass, signoff, and done-state language for trustworthy progress.

opportunity_zones.zone: calm control and enterprise trust without enterprise bloat
opportunity_zones.direction: Short, composed, legible names that feel dependable without sounding like complianceware.

positioning_summary: Avoid literal AI-agent and workflow-engine naming. Explore names that make coordinated software work feel evidenced, bound, navigable, and calmly complete.
